parsed.headline: Israeli military operations in Hebron displace thousands following fatal checkpoint attack

pages.text: Israeli military operations in Hebron, the largest city in the West Bank, have displaced thousands of residents following a gun attack on October 23, 2026, that killed two soldiers at a military checkpoint. According to Hebron municipality authorities, the ongoing operation, which began on October 24, 2026, has displaced 3,189 people, including more than 200 infants. The municipality reported these figures in a statement on Monday. Following the October 23 attack, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich visited the site and vowed retribution. Netanyahu warned of imminent military operations in the West Bank on a scale not seen in nearly 60 years. Within hours of the attack, the city of 250,000 people was sealed off, and the Farsh al-Hawa neighborhood, located near the checkpoint, was flattened. By the morning of October 25, 2026, an industrial area containing car workshops and a ceramics plant had been reduced to rubble. In the Ein Deir Baha neighborhood, which was allegedly home to at least one of the two gunmen killed during the October 23 shootout, residents were ordered by military vehicle loudspeakers to vacate their homes for their own safety. Fahed Ahmaro, a local mosque imam, reported that he was forced to move 30 family members to another part of Hebron after the army blew up the gates to his house. On October 25, 2026, images showed a convoy of Israeli military and police vehicles moving through streets in Hebron that were blocked to civilian traffic.

parsed.headline: President Mahama arrives in Moscow for third Russia–Africa Summit

pages.text: President John Dramani Mahama of Ghana arrived in Moscow on Monday to lead a delegation to the third Russia–Africa Summit. Hosted by Russian President Vladimir Putin and scheduled for October 28–29, 2026, the summit is expected to include more than 30 African heads of state and government. The forum is anticipated to focus on peace diplomacy, security cooperation, and equitable economic partnerships. Upon arrival, the President was met by Russian government officials and Ghana’s Ambassador to Russia, Dr. Koma Steem Jehu-Appiah, along with embassy staff. Mahama traveled to Moscow from Ethiopia prior to the summit's commencement. During the visit, the President is expected to participate in plenary sessions, an Economic and Humanitarian Forum, and a kente exhibition organized by the Russia Ghana Parliamentary Forum. He is also scheduled to grant audience to various Russian state institutions and businesses. Additionally, the Russian University of Transport and the Peoples’ Friendship University of Russia are set to confer honorary doctorate degrees upon him during separate ceremonies.

Speaking at the Financial Times Africa Summit on October 21, President Mahama stated he intends to use the Moscow visit to press for a ceasefire in the four-year-old Russia–Ukraine war. He framed this objective within Ghana's non-aligned foreign policy, describing the nation as having cordial relations with the United States, the European Union, China, and Russia. Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa confirmed that President Mahama is expected to hold a high-level bilateral meeting with President Putin on the margins of the summit to deepen relations between the two countries.

parsed.headline: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wins Brazilian presidential runoff as Flávio Bolsonaro seeks annulment

pages.text: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a fourth nonconsecutive term on October 25, 2026, defeating far-right Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in a presidential runoff. Lula received 51.79% of the valid votes, totaling approximately 64.26 million ballots, while Bolsonaro received 48.21%, or 59.83 million votes. This result represents a margin of roughly 4.4 million votes and a reversal from the October 4 first round, in which Bolsonaro led Lula by approximately 2.2 million votes. Lula is the first candidate since Brazil's return to democracy in 1985 to win a presidential runoff after finishing second in the opening round. Following the announcement, Lula vowed that dictatorship and fascism would not return to Brazil while addressing supporters in São Paulo. The victory was met with celebrations in Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo, where supporters gathered in the streets. Global figures, including Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum, Canadian Governor General Mary Simon, and U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders, offered congratulations, while U.S. Congressman Ro Khanna called for President Donald Trump to respect the results. Conversely, Donald Trump Jr. criticized the outcome regarding a voting extension. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, refused to concede and called for the election to be annulled. Bolsonaro described the decision to extend voting hours as an “unacceptable” and “dirty trick.” The extension, ordered by Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin, was requested by both candidates due to heavy rains and reports that buses had been pulled from circulation, which Lula claimed barred citizens from voting. However, the president of the electoral court, Justice Kassio Nunes Marques, stated the extension did not affect the result, and leaders of the supreme court and congress have recognized the re-election. An analysis by the newspaper Folha de S.Paulo indicated that only 34,330 votes, or 0.03% of the total, were cast after the original 5 p.m. closing time, a figure described as insignificant compared to the 4.4 million-vote margin.

parsed.headline: Bank of Canada faces conflicting economic indicators

pages.text: The Canadian economy is currently experiencing two distinct issues that present a challenge for the Bank of Canada. According to CBC Canada, inflation recently rose to 3.1 per cent, though price increases have so far been contained to the energy sector while core measures remained subdued. While inflation is rising, the economy is also characterized by weak growth, and the impact of the latest tranche of tariffs has not yet been measured. These competing factors create a dilemma for the central bank: weak growth typically prompts interest rate cuts to spur activity, whereas rising inflation often prompts rate increases to slow the economy and control prices.

parsed.headline: Ghana Climate Literacy Portal seeks to expand resources for young Africans

pages.text: The Ghana Climate Literacy Portal (GCLP) is working to provide young Africans with knowledge and resources to respond to climate change. The digital platform is being highlighted at the Regional Conference of Youth Africa (RCOY Africa) in Accra, where advocates are discussing environmental solutions and ways to increase youth participation in climate policy. Since its launch last year, the portal has attracted more than 5,000 learners, according to Mary-Ann Essilfie-Arhin, the leader of the GCLP. Essilfie-Arhin stated the platform is designed to connect climate science, policy, advocacy, and practical solutions through digital learning. The GCLP team is currently looking to expand course offerings and introduce language tools to reach French- and Swahili-speaking communities to address language barriers in accessing educational resources.

At the RCOY Africa conference, Saustine Lusanzu, a Tanzanian climate advocate and founder of the Earth Care Foundation, described the portal as an opportunity for African youth to build the knowledge necessary to lead environmental change. Lusanzu stated that access to reliable climate learning materials could assist young people in moving from awareness to taking practical action within their communities. The RCOY Africa conference serves as a platform for young leaders to develop proposals and contribute to a shared youth statement regarding climate policy and decision-making priorities.

parsed.headline: Student-led initiative targets low voter turnout in Peel region, Canada

pages.text: A student-led initiative is working to address barriers to civic engagement in an effort to reverse low voter turnout trends in the Peel region ahead of Ontario's municipal election on October 19, 2026. The community group, Voice the Vote, was co-launched by the Democratic Engagement Exchange (DEE) at Toronto Metropolitan University and United Way Greater Toronto. Through outreach, regular events, and educational tools, the group aims to increase attention to local politics in the Peel, York, and Toronto regions. Abby Tait, the group's senior public affairs manager, stated that the initiative aims to center community voices to drive conversations about elections following provincial and federal snap elections. Voice the Vote utilizes a 'vote pop-up toolkit' featuring a mock ballot and voting screen to engage people with municipal issues before directing them to candidate information resources.

Data from the Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO) shows that the 2022 municipal election reached a record-low provincial average voter turnout of 32.9 per cent, down from approximately 38 per cent in 2018. In the Peel region, 2022 turnout rates were lower than the provincial average: 24.5 per cent in Brampton, 31.7 per cent in Caledon, and just under 22 per cent in Mississauga. Members of Voice the Vote have identified a lack of awareness regarding the role of municipal governments and difficulties in accessing reliable, accessible information about candidates and platforms as factors contributing to lower voter numbers.

parsed.headline: Police block cultural activists’ protest in Dhaka, Bangladesh

pages.text: Police prevented cultural activists from holding a planned human chain protest in the Dhanmondi area of Dhaka, Bangladesh, on October 26, 2026. The activists, organized under the banner of “Protesting Artistes and People,” had gathered in front of Meena Bazar at Dhanmondi 27 around 4:00 pm to protest what they described as attacks and aggression by individuals acting in the name of the Tawhidi Janata against Baul music and other cultural events in various parts of the country. The protest specifically aimed to address the obstruction of female Baul singers from performing in Sunamganj. Prior to the gathering, more than 100 police personnel had taken positions in the area starting at 3:30 pm.

During the encounter, theatre activist Sumana Islam approached the police to ask if the human chain would be permitted. According to reports, police stated they had received instructions from higher authorities to ensure participants did not chant provocative slogans or make provocative remarks. When police noted that a previous group at the same location had chanted the slogan “Joy Bangla,” Dipak Shil, a former president of the Bangladesh Chhatra Union, questioned if the slogan had become spoiled, noting it was used during the July uprising. Following an argument, police detained Shil and placed him in a vehicle. Sumana Islam, who attempted to stop the detention, alleged that officers confronted her aggressively and manhandled her.

parsed.headline: Syria and Qatari firm sign $147 million agreement to upgrade 170 km road

pages.text: Authorities in the Syrian Arab Republic signed an agreement on Monday with the Qatari firm Al-Mohannadi for Roads to rehabilitate and expand a 170 km road connecting the Al-Busayri junction in Damascus to the Al-Tanf border crossing with Iraq. According to the Syrian Arab News Agency, officials stated the project is part of efforts to rebuild transport infrastructure and strengthen regional trade links. The highway runs through Syria’s eastern desert and connects Iraq to Syrian Mediterranean ports. Under the agreement, construction is expected to take 900 days. The Syrian General Establishment for Road Transport is the other party to the $147 million deal. Transport Minister Yarub Badr said the agreement is part of a road rehabilitation program launched in summer 2026 to restore key routes.

Finance Minister Mohammed Yisr Barnieh stated that the Syrian government has allocated $193 million for major road projects in the 2026 budget. Additionally, $450 million has been set aside in the 2027 draft budget. Barnieh also noted that the government has proposed allocating $200 million to railway projects next year.

pages.text: The Bangladesh Medical Tourism Association (BMTA) has elected a new executive committee for a one-year term. According to a statement reported by The Financial Express Bangladesh, the election activities were led by Election Commissioner Dr. Mohammad Jamshed Alam and took place on Sunday at a city hotel. Khandaker Sitabur Rahman, the founder and CEO of Khandaker Medical Tourism, was elected General Secretary of the association.

The newly elected committee includes Vice Presidents Shabbir Ahmad Tamim, co-founder and CEO of MediAider, and AMR Mojumder Liton, CEO of WCA Medical Evacuation Service. Ainul Tareq Nobel was elected Joint Secretary (Finance), and Md. Abdullah Al Atiq was elected Joint Secretary (Admin). Other executive members of the committee are Nazmul Islam Rafi, Abdur Rashid, Daud Arman, Mohammad Ariful Islam, S. Arif Hossain, and Gias Mohammad Azizul Haque.

parsed.headline: Bank of Ghana researchers develop AI-powered inflation tracking system

pages.text: Researchers at the Bank of Ghana (BoG) have developed an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered inflation tracking system called e-Inflation, which is capable of providing near real-time estimates of consumer price movements, according to a study. The system uses Big Data and AI techniques to monitor prices across online platforms to generate inflation estimates before official figures are released. Currently, official inflation data in Ghana are compiled through conventional price collection methods and are typically published after the end of each reference month. The study noted that while delays are necessary for data validation and compilation, they can limit the ability of policymakers and market participants to respond quickly to changing economic conditions. The e-Inflation model relies on machine learning algorithms and web-scraping tools to collect and analyze large volumes of price data from websites and other digital sources, tracking goods and services frequently purchased by consumers.

The study found that the e-Inflation measure closely tracked Ghana’s official inflation rate during the study period, demonstrating an ability to mirror official trends. Researchers suggested that these AI-driven estimates could serve as a reliable complement to traditional statistical methods and provide early signals of changes in the cost of living. The researchers stated the model could assist policymakers, businesses, and investors in accessing timely information to improve economic decision-making. Specifically, the study noted that real-time indicators could be useful for the Bank of Ghana’s Monetary Policy Committee, which makes interest rate decisions based on current and expected inflation developments. The study also highlighted that the increasing use of online platforms by consumers and businesses creates opportunities to collect price information at a higher frequency and lower cost.
